title: 9.5 Probability of Disjoint and Overlapping Events

icans: I can tell whether two events are disjoint or overlapping.
I can find P(A or B) when A and B are disjoint.
I can find P(A or B) when A and B overlap.

vocab: events that can’t __________ at the same time
events that have at least one __________ in common

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem: A card is chosen from cards numbered 1 to 10. What is the probability that the number is less than 3 or greater than 8?

notes: Why subtract?: I subtract P(A and B) so the overlap is counted only _______________.

blocks.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 play a sport, 12 are in the band, and 5 do both. What is the probability that a student plays a sport or is in the band?

At a theater, 60% of the audience are adults. 30% of the adults and 50% of the children say they would see the movie again. What is the probability that a randomly chosen audience member would see it again?
You roll a die. What is the probability of rolling an even number or a number greater than 4?

tickets.stem: You roll a die. Are “rolling an even number” and “rolling a 3” disjoint or overlapping?
A and B are disjoint, P(A) = 0.4, and P(B) = 0.3. Find P(A or B).
